references.text: Turtledoves or young pigeons are mentioned as acceptable burnt offerings, the same bird species as in the guilt offering for the poor.
Shows a further reduction in sacrifice requirements for those who cannot afford birds, demonstrating God's grace toward the poor.
The same provision of two turtledoves or two young pigeons applies to those who cannot afford a lamb, used for purification after childbirth.
A parallel provision for lepers who cannot afford the usual offering, with the same bird sacrifice as an alternative.
Describes the use of turtledoves or young pigeons as sin offerings and burnt offerings for poor lepers.
The Nazirite vow concludes with the same type of bird offering for those who cannot afford larger animals.
Mary and Joseph offered two turtledoves or two young pigeons at Jesus' presentation in the temple, showing that they used the poverty provision from the Mosaic Law.
Christ became poor for our sake, reflecting the theme that God provides for the poor within the sacrificial system.
